key_concepts: Plant propagation is growing plants from seeds or plant parts.
Sexual propagation involves the union of pollen and ovule to form seeds.
Seeds are sown in soil or growing medium to germinate and grow.
Pollination is essential for sexual propagation.
Asexual propagation grows new plants from parts of an existing plant.
Asexual propagation produces genetically identical offspring.
Cuttings use a stem or root piece placed in a medium to regenerate a new plant.
Grafting joins parts of two plants so they grow as one.
Layering roots a branch while it is still attached to the parent plant.
Division separates a parent plant into parts that each grow into a new plant.
Environment plays a critical role in propagation success.
